subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Dodging Social Media Bullets, Fancy AeroPress, John Candy, and Quotes

bullets.title: Everything Is Television
bullets.creator: Derek Thompson
bullets.note: . This is a superb piece. If you are online, you should read it. If you create online, you should read it twice. If you’re in a rush, just read the Meta anti-monopoly comments and look at the graphs. Derek’s observations and citations largely explain my deliberate down-scaling of video over the last few years, in addition to concerns around [audience capture](https://www.gurwinder.blog/p/the-perils-of-audience-capture) and privacy. Last, it’s always bothered me when techno-optimists insist AI will make the masses all a leisure class with more time than ever before for learning, knitting, or whatever. Putting aside the fact that most of them are big investors in AI, nothing has ever delivered on that promise and prediction (cue: Industrial Revolution). This piece makes a compelling case that AI will make time feel scarcer, not more abundant. In a future 5BF or blog post, I might describe how I’m setting up personal safeguards against this.

bullets.title: Glass and Metal AeroPress
bullets.note: I [wrote a lot](https://x.com/tferriss/status/1592547686049251328) about the amazing AeroPress in [_The 4-Hour Chef_](https://www.amazon.com/4-Hour-Chef-Cooking-Learning-Anything/dp/1328519163/), but I always had reservations about putting hot water into a plastic container. I’ve increasingly tried to avoid plastics, especially in combination with heat (see this [Dr. Rhonda Patrick](https://tim.blog/2025/07/24/dr-rhonda-patrick/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit) podcast for more). This new and premium version of the AeroPress avoids the plastic problem altogether. If you want to go the extra mile, pair it with their [reusable titanium-coated stainless steel filter](https://aeropress.com/products/aeropress-gold-tone-filter-standard). It ain’t cheap, but if you’re a coffee snob, it might be worth the ride.

bullets.title: John Candy: I Like Me
bullets.note: As someone whose childhood was saturated with love for John Candy, this doc hit the mark. The first ~15 minutes start slow, and then it quickly ramps up. From the description: “From director Colin Hanks and producer Ryan Reynolds comes _John Candy: I Like Me_. Those who knew John best \[e.g., Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, Catherine O’Hara\] share his story, in their own words, through never-before-seen archival footage, imagery, and interviews. It’s a documentary of the life, career, and loss of one of the most beloved actors of all time.” You can watch the trailer [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PrcQRsrBcCk).
